key_insight: A fly-inspired vision architecture that preserves parallel ON/OFF pathways and recurrent graph interactions can scale from small image tasks to large natural and biomedical vision benchmarks with competitive accuracy.
clinical_relevance: This work suggests biologically structured computer vision models may improve medical image classification and MRI-based age estimation while using fewer parameters than standard CNN baselines.
method: Built ConnectomeX around FlyVision, a trainable architecture inspired by the Drosophila visual connectome.
Kept core biological motifs: parallel ON/OFF processing, recurrent computation, and population-level graph interaction.
Extended FlyVision to 2D classification and 3D brain age prediction by fusing slice-level MRI estimates with confidence-modulated Gaussian voting.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports results across MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-1K, skin-disease classification, chest radiography, and 433 held-out MRI scans, including top-1 accuracy, AUROC, and MAE comparisons against ResNet18.
watch_item: Performance is promising but still task-dependent, and some gains come with added architectural complexity that may affect training and deployment reproducibility.
paper_title: From the Drosophila Visual Connectome to General-Purpose Computer Vision
